t: Minimum Number of Groups to Create a Valid Assignment
o: Group equal-valued balls into boxes; all box sizes must differ by at most 1, i.e., every box has size k or k+1 for some global k. Minimize the number of boxes. Only the frequency of each value matters. Example 1: frequencies {3:3, 2:2} — k=2 splits 3→[3] wait, sizes 2 and 3: 3 = one box of 3, 2 = one box of 2 → 2 boxes. Example 2: {10:3, 3:1, 1:2} — no k lets 3 fit with 1s and 2s together consistently, so 4 boxes. Strategy: for each candidate k, check every frequency c can be written as a·k + b·(k+1), and sum the minimal part counts; take the best k.
k: Only frequencies matter; values themselves are irrelevant.
A count c is splittable into parts of size k or k+1 iff some a ∈ [0, min(c//k, k)] makes (c − a·k) divisible by (k+1) — residues cycle with period k+1, so checking a ≤ k suffices.

a.n: Approach 1: Try every box size k
a.i: For each k from 1 to max frequency, verify each count is representable with parts k/k+1 and accumulate minimal boxes; answer is the minimum over feasible k.
s: For each k, for each count c, scan a = 0..min(c//k, k) for (c − a·k) % (k+1) == 0
If all counts feasible, candidate = Σ a + (c−a·k)/(k+1); take min
a.t: O(F · K²) worst case where F = distinct values, K = max frequency — fast in practice due to early breaks

a.i: Same enumeration but iterate k descending and prune any k whose partial total already reaches the best; also skip a-values whose remainder goes negative early. This passes comfortably and is simple to explain.
s: Sort frequencies descending so failures happen fast
Enumerate k with pruning on partial sums
a.t: Same worst case, much faster with pruning

w: The key lemma to state clearly: residues of c − a·k mod (k+1) cycle with period k+1 in a, so scanning a up to k suffices. Pitfall: forgetting that k itself is a valid box size (parts are k OR k+1, not just k+1), and trying k larger than the max frequency (never feasible). Follow-up: return an actual assignment, not just the count.
